> "Affiliate" means, with respect to any Person, any other Person that directly or indirectly controls, is controlled by, or is under common control with, such Person.
> "Business Day" means any day other than a Saturday, Sunday, or other day on which commercial banks in New York, New York, or Wilmington, Delaware, are authorized or required by law to remain closed.

## Transfer Restrictions – STRA (Share Transfer Restriction Agreement)
Section 2 imposes a series of mechanisms to control share transfers: (a) a Right of First Refusal (ROFR) requiring a shareholder receiving a third‑party offer to first offer the shares to the other shareholders on identical terms; (b) a Right of First Offer (ROFO) obligating a selling shareholder to first solicit the other shareholders; (c) a Tag‑Along right triggered when a shareholder sells more than 20 % of its shares, allowing the others to participate pro‑rata; (d) a Drag‑Along right that, upon approval by shareholders holding at least 75 % of the equity, compels the remaining shareholders to sell; and (e) a carve‑out permitting transfers to Affiliates without ROFR/ROFO constraints.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> 2.1 Right of First Refusal (ROFR). If any Shareholder receives a third-party offer to purchase its shares, it must first offer them to the other Shareholders on the same terms.
> 2.2 Right of First Offer (ROFO). A Shareholder wishing to sell must first offer its shares to the other Shareholders.
> 2.3 Tag-Along. If a Shareholder sells more than 20% of its shares, other Shareholders can participate on a pro-rata basis.
> 2.4 Drag-Along. If 75% of shareholders approve a sale, they can force the remaining Shareholders to sell.
> 2.5 Permitted Transfers. ROFR/ROFO restrictions do not apply to transfers to Affiliates.

The recitals set out Tata's public disclosures of a diversified clean‑energy portfolio and its need for regulatory, siting and programme‑management support for rooftop solar and EV‑charging expansion. The commercial backdrop requires structured advisory services with measurable deliverables, confidentiality, IP ownership and compliance with the Tata Code of Conduct and all applicable laws.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> This Services Agreement is entered into between Tata Power Renewable Energy Limited and Helios Grid Advisory Private Limited.
> Public Tata business disclosures ... describe a diversified power portfolio, an extensive clean-energy platform, and India's largest EV charging network; the contemplated engagement supports disciplined scaling, permitting, and customer‑facing implementation.

## Definitions and Interpretation – SA-Helios (Service Agreement)
Clause 1 defines that references to the Agreement include recitals, schedules, annexures, statements of work, change orders and any written amendments signed by the Parties. Headings are for convenience only. References to law include amendments, reenactments, subordinate legislation and binding governmental directions. In case of conflict, the main body prevails unless a statement of work expressly states a clause supersedes the main body. "Days" means calendar days unless otherwise stated.

**Supporting Quotes:**

> Where there is any conflict between the main body of this Agreement and a statement of work, the main body shall prevail unless the statement of work expressly states that a specific clause is intended to supersede the main body for that workstream.

Clause 2 obliges the Service Provider to perform the services described in the relevant statement of work, including site diligence reports, regulatory matrices, interconnection risk reviews, vendor mobilisation dashboards and compliance exception trackers. Clause 10 obliges each Party to protect the other’s Confidential Information with at least a reasonable degree of care, not to disclose except with consent or as required by law, and to continue the duty for two years after termination. Return or destruction of Confidential Information is required upon termination.

## Term and Termination – SA1-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 9.1 sets the initial term to one year from execution, subject to mutual written extension. Termination may occur by mutual agreement, force majeure, or unilaterally by TATA with 30‑day notice, for breach (10‑day cure), or upon insolvency events (60‑day cure).

**Supporting Quotes:**
> "9.1 This Agreement shall be effective ... and shall remain valid for a period of 1 year, unless mutually extended by the Parties in writing or terminated earlier..."

> "(d) by TATA ... if the Service Provider is in breach ... not remedied within 10 (ten) days of receipt of notice..."

Clause 13 obligates the Service Provider to indemnify TATA and its affiliates against claims arising from breaches of representations, obligations, IP infringement, or negligent acts.

(ii) breach of any obligation ... (iii) claims for infringement of Intellectual Property Rights of third parties; and/or (iv) misconduct or negligent acts..."

Clause 14 limits both Parties from liability for indirect, consequential loss, loss of profit, goodwill, business opportunity or anticipated savings.

## Assignment and Sub‑contracting – SA1-Tata (Service Agreement)

The Service Provider shall continue to be liable to TATA for any sub‑contracted or assigned work."

## Dispute Resolution – SA1-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 12 requires initial escalation to senior representatives for amicable settlement; if unresolved within 30 days, disputes are referred to arbitration under the Indian Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, with three arbitrators (one each appointed by TATA and Service Provider, the third by the two). The seat is Mumbai, language English, and the award is final and binding.

Clause 16 contains boilerplate provisions on severability, waiver, amendment, counterpart execution, exclusivity of rights, data privacy compliance, anti‑corruption warranties, and survival of key clauses after termination.

## Schedule I – Services – SA1-Tata (Service Agreement)

## Schedule II – Service Fee – SA1-Tata (Service Agreement)
Schedule II sets the fixed retainer amount payable from the Effective Date (exact figure redacted in the excerpt) and notes that the amount is exclusive of applicable taxes. It also outlines the supervision fee of 5% on third‑party work and travel expense reimbursement subject to TATA approval.

> "Service Provider will be paid the fixed ... (Above cost is exclusive of applicable taxes)"

## Scope of Services – SA‑Tata (Service Agreement)
The Agreement obliges the Consultant to provide the services described in the Schedule (referred to as ‘Services’). The clause is introductory and does not list specific deliverables, but it creates the contractual basis for all subsequent performance obligations.

> The Consultant shall provide the Services to the Client as described in this Agreement.

## Term and Termination – SA‑Tata (Service Agreement)
The Agreement commences on 1° April 2023 and remains in force until 31°* March 2024 unless terminated earlier. Mutual termination requires 60 days’ written notice; termination by the Client triggers payment for accepted milestones and proportionate fees for incomplete milestones based on hours spent.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> The effective date of this Agreement shall be 1° April 2023 and the same shall be valid till 31°* March 2024, unless terminated earlier as per the terms of this Agreement.
> Mutual agreement to terminate by giving 60 days’ written notice to the other Party for any reason whatsoever
> Upon termination intimated by Client, Consultant shall be eligible and Client shall pay to Consultant fees for the milestones or deliverables accepted.
> Further Consultant shall also be entitled to proportionate payment of fees for incomplete milestones, which amount shall be calculated on the basis of Consulting hours spent by Consultant on such Milestone.

## Warranties – SA‑Tata (Service Agreement)
The Consultant warrants reasonable care, skill, diligence, timely delivery, compliance with applicable laws, and possession of all necessary licences throughout the term.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> Consultant represents and warrants to Client that: It will use all reasonable care, skill and diligence in carrying out the services;
> It will supply the services in a timely manner;
> In supplying the Services, it will comply with all applicable regulations, laws and legislations;
> It has all licenses, authorizations, consents, approvals and permits required by applicable law in order to perform its obligations under this agreement

## Independent Contractor – SA‑Tata (Service Agreement)
The Parties acknowledge that the Consultant is an independent contractor; no partnership, joint venture, or authority to bind the other party is created.

**Supporting Quotes:**

> Constitute the Parties as partners, joint venturers or co‑owners for the purpose of this Agreement;

## Taxes – SA‑Tata (Service Agreement)
The Consultant must issue GST‑compliant e‑invoices; any non‑compliant invoice will be rejected. The Consultant must remit GST, and any loss of input tax credit to the Client due to the Consultant’s non‑compliance is payable by the Consultant, including interest and penalties. All payments are subject to TDS/CTDS as per the Income‑Tax Act, 1961.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> (a) The Consultant shall ensure that all invoices issued by it are in the format specified by GST Act and Rules including the e‑invoicing requirements, any non‑compliant invoices shall be rejected by Client.
> (b) The Consultant must remit the GST amount to the respective authority in accordance with the GST laws.
> (c) Any cost, liability, dues, penalty, fees, interest … which accrues to the Client … due to default on the part of Consultant shall be borne by Consultant.
> (d) All payments under the agreement shall be subject to applicable Tax Deduction / Collection at Source as per the provisions of the Income‑tax Act, 1961

## Fee and Payment – SA‑Tata (Service Agreement)
Fees are payable in Indian Rupees. The Consultant invoices after each milestone; invoices must indicate milestones achieved. Payments are due within 30 days of receipt. Fees are fixed for the term, subject only to mutual written amendment. Purchases of stock images, videos and music are billed as actuals with prior written approval.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> Client shall effect payments to Consultant after acceptance by Client of the invoices submitted by Consultant … upon the achievement of the corresponding milestones

> Fees shall remain fixed and is not subject to any adjustment or revision during the term of the agreement, except as otherwise mutually agreed between the parties.
> Client shall effect payment of Consultant's invoice within 30 days following receipt of the same.

## Confidentiality – SA‑Tata (Service Agreement)
Both Parties must keep Confidential Information confidential, use at least reasonable care, limit disclosure to representatives on a need‑to‑know basis, and obtain written consent before third‑party disclosure. Exceptions include public information, prior lawful possession, third‑party disclosures without restriction, independent development, and compelled disclosure with prior notice. Obligations survive termination.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> For purposes of this Agreement, “Confidential Information” shall mean and include all information and materials … being disclosed or observed …

> The provisions of this clause shall survive even after the termination of this Agreement.

## Intellectual Property Ownership – SA‑Tata (Service Agreement)
All work product created specifically for the Client becomes the Client’s property upon full and final payment. The Consultant retains copies subject to confidentiality. The Consultant irrevocably assigns all worldwide IP rights, free from encumbrances, for the full term of each right.

> Such work product shall become the property of Client upon full and final payment to Consultant, subject to the provisions of this agreement
> The Consultant hereby irrevocably, absolutely and perpetually assigns to the Client all right, title and interest … in respect of the work product … free from encumbrances of any kind for the full term of each and every such intellectual property right

## Indemnity – SA‑Tata (Service Agreement)
Each Party indemnifies the other against all claims, costs, losses, damages and expenses arising from the indemnifying Party’s negligent or unlawful acts, except to the extent such liability arises from the other Party’s negligence. The indemnity is unlimited and survives termination.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> Consultant agree to indemnify the Client … from any … actions, claims, … which may be brought against the Client as a result of any act or omission, proven negligence or otherwise, by the Consultant, except … that such liability arose out of a negligent or unlawful acts … on the part of the Client.
> Client agrees to indemnify the Consultant … as a result of any act or omission, negligence or otherwise, by the client, except … that such liability arose out of a proven negligent or unlawful acts … on the part of the Consultant.
> The parties are fully responsible and liable, without any limitation, for any loss, damage, injury, death, costs or expenses suffered by the other party …

## Force Majeure – SA‑Tata (Service Agreement)
Neither Party is liable for delays caused by events beyond control (riot, pandemic, strike, theft, war, acts of God). The affected Party must notify the other in writing promptly and provide particulars. If the event persists for three continuous months, the Agreement terminates.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> Neither the Client, nor the Consultant, shall be liable for any default, delay or lapse occurring due to ‘SJ events beyond their control including riot, pandemic, strike, theft, war, or other acts of God.
> The Party so affected shall use its best efforts to remove the cause of non‑performance … if the force majeure event continues for a period of three months continuously, the Agreement shall stand terminated.

## Modification – SA‑Tata (Service Agreement)
Any amendment to the Agreement must be made in writing, signed by authorized officials of both Parties, and will have prospective effect only.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> Any changes in the terms and conditions contained herein shall have effect only prospectively, and shall be by mutual consent and be valid only if recorded in writing and signed by the authorized officials of the Client and the Consultant.

## Notices – SA‑Tata (Service Agreement)
All communications must be in writing and are deemed received when delivered in person, confirmed fax, five days after registered post, confirmed private courier delivery, or upon electronic mail transmission.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> All notices and communications between the Parties hereto shall be in writing … and deemed received: (i) when delivered in person; or (ii) upon confirmed transmission by facsimile device; or (iii) five (5) days after postmarked by Registered Post A. D.; or (iv) date of confirmed delivery by private courier service; or (vi) when addressed to the other party by electronic mail

## Cessation of Rights and Obligations – SA‑Tata (Service Agreement)
Upon termination or expiry, all rights and obligations cease except accrued rights, confidentiality (Clause 8), IP ownership (Clause 9), and any rights under governing law.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> Upon termination of this agreement … all rights and obligations of the Parties shall cease, except (a) such rights and obligations as may have accrued at the date of termination or expiration; (b) the obligations under Clauses 8 and 9 contained herein; (c) any right that a party may have under the governing law.

## Limitation of Liability – SA‑Tata (Service Agreement)
Each Party’s liability for damages is capped at the amount billed by the Service Provider to the customer in the two invoices preceding the cause of action. Service level credits are excluded. The Service Provider is not liable for damages caused by the Customer’s failure to perform.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> Each party's liability to the other party for damages, shall be limited to the actual amount billed by Service Provider to customer in the last two invoices raised prior to the cause of action first arose.
> In no event will the Service Provider be liable for any damages caused by customer's failure to perform its responsibilities under this Agreement.

## Assignment – SA‑Tata (Service Agreement)
Neither Party may assign the Agreement without the other Party’s prior written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld; any unauthorized assignment is void and a material breach.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> Neither Party may assign this Agreement without the other Party’s prior written consent, which consent will not be unreasonably withheld.
> Any attempted assignment … without the other party's prior written consent will be void and will constitute a material breach of this Agreement.

## Non‑Solicitation – SA‑Tata (Service Agreement)
During the term and for one year thereafter, neither Party shall solicit or employ the other Party’s employees without consent, except via general advertisement.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> Neither Party shall solicit or otherwise offer employment to an employee of the other Party … during the term of this agreement or … for a period of one year thereafter, without the consent of the other party.

## Governing Law and Dispute Resolution – SA‑Tata (Service Agreement)
The Agreement is governed by Indian law. Disputes are first to be resolved by mutual discussion; failing that, they are referred to arbitration under the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996, with a sole arbitrator appointed by the Parties, seated in Mumbai, conducted in English. The award is final and binding. The Parties also submit to the jurisdiction of Mumbai courts.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> The Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of India.
> In the event of disputes … the same shall be resolved by mutual discussions and negotiations, failing which … shall be referred to arbitration, to be conducted by a sole arbitrator mutually appointed by the Parties.
> The arbitration proceedings shall be conducted as per the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, 1996 … The venue of arbitration shall be Mumbai and the arbitration proceedings shall be conducted in English language.
> Subject to above, the Parties hereby submit to the jurisdiction of the Courts at Mumbai.

## Counterparts – SA‑Tata (Service Agreement)
The Agreement may be executed in multiple counterparts, each of which is an original, together constituting one instrument.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> This Contract may be executed in any number of counterparts and by the parties hereto in separate counterparts, each of which when so executed and delivered shall be deemed an original, but all such counterparts together shall constitute one and the same instrument.

## Parties – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
The Agreement is entered into between Tata Sons Private Limited, a company incorporated under the laws of India with its registered office at Bombay House, Mumbai, and the Service Provider (identified only as "Service Provider" in the document). Each party is referred to individually as a "Party" and collectively as the "Parties". The opening clause establishes the identity, corporate status and address of Tata Sons, and incorporates the Service Provider’s heirs, executors and administrators.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> "Tata Sons Private Limited, a company incorporated under laws of India and having its registered office at Bombay House, 24 Homi Mody Street, Mumbai 400 001 (hereinafter referred to as \"TATA\")"
> "(hereinafter, referred to as \"Service Provider\" which expression shall include unless repugnant to the context, his/her heirs, executors and administrators)\"

## Definitions – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 1.1 provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Agreement, including "Agreement", "Arbitral Tribunal", "Confidential Information", "Effective Date", "Force Majeure Event", "Intellectual Property", "Service Fee", and "TATA Manager". These definitions set the interpretative framework for the parties’ rights and obligations.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> "\"Agreement\" means this Agreement, together with the Schedules and Annexures attached hereto, as may be amended from time to time;"
> "\"Confidential Information\" of any Party shall include without limitation any and all materials, trade secrets, intellectual property, know-how, formulae, processes, algorithms, ideas, strategies, inventions, data, innovations, network configurations, system architecture, designs, flow charts, drawings, proprietary information, business and marketing plans, financial information, operational information, business methods, underwriting ideas and information and all other non‑public information, material or data relating to the past, current and /or future business and operations of such Party;"

## Scope of Services – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 2 obligates the Service Provider to render the Services from the Effective Date in accordance with Schedule I. The Services are described as a comprehensive audit of the Tata Review’s magazine design and editorial approach, with detailed sub‑scopes for design and content audit. The clause emphasizes that time is of the essence and that the Service Provider must obtain all necessary permits and licenses.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> "The Parties hereby agree that Service Provider shall, from the Effective Date, in terms of this Agreement, render services to TATA in accordance with the details and timelines, as more particularly set out in Schedule I hereto (\"Services\")."
> "The Service Provider acknowledges that time is of essence for this Agreement and undertakes to provide quality professional services in a timely manner."

## Service Fee – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 3.1 states that the Service Provider will be paid the fee set out in Schedule II. Payments are exclusive of GST, which the Service Provider must mark separately on the invoice. Clause 3.2 requires tax deduction at source where applicable, with TDS certificates to be furnished. Schedule II further details reimbursement of travel expenses and a 20 % sourcing fee on stock photographs.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> "In consideration of the Service Provider providing the Services, a fee as set out in Schedule II (\"Service Fee\") shall be payable to the Service Provider."
> "Payments shall be due within 30 days from the Invoice date."
> "Photographs purchased from stock libraries will be billed at actuals plus a 20 per cent sourcing fee."

## Project Management – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 4 allows Tata to assign a "TATA Manager" to coordinate with the Service Provider. Any change of the TATA Manager must be communicated in writing at least fourteen days in advance. This clause creates a single point of contact for performance review and problem resolution.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> "TATA may assign a representative (\"TATA Manager\") for coordination with the Service Provider Manager to review performance of this Agreement, resolutions of problems and other activities to facilitate success of this arrangement."
> "TATA shall send written notice to the Service Provider 14 (fourteen) days in advance about change of TATA Manager at anytime during the term of this Agreement."

## Representations and Warranties – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 5.1 contains the Service Provider’s warranties that it has the requisite rights to provide the Services, that its performance will not infringe any third‑party IP, that it complies with all applicable laws, and that it possesses all necessary licences and expertise. These representations form the basis for the indemnity obligations in Clause 11.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> "The Service Provider represents and warrants to TATA that: (a) it has the requisite rights, power and authority to provide the Services... and that possession and use of such information, specifications, data, work for hire and Services shall, at no point in time, ... constitute an infringement... of any patent, copyright, trade secret, or any other Intellectual Property Right of any third party;"
> "(b) the execution and delivery of this Agreement by it, the performance by it of its obligations hereunder and compliance by it with the provisions hereof will not violate, contravene or breach or create a default under any agreement, instrument, charter or by‑law provision, statute, regulation, judgment, ordinance, decree, writ, injunction or applicable law;"

## Intellectual Property – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 6 confirms that each Party retains ownership of its pre‑existing IP, but the Services are performed on a "work for hire" basis, giving TATA ownership of all IP created under the Agreement, including modifications and derivative works. The Service Provider must execute documents to vest those rights and may not use the work product for any other client.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> "The Service Provider acknowledges and agrees that the Services are performed and provided under this Agreement on a \"work for hire\" basis and TATA shall own all Intellectual Property rights contained in and with respect to the Services..."
> "The Service Provider shall not use any work product resulting from the Services and/or Intellectual Property of TATA in any manner whatsoever for itself or for any client other than TATA, at anytime."

## Force Majeure – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)

The JV will operate under safety‑first protocols, approval gates for second‑life deployment, environmental compliance audits, and reserved matters for plant expansion and technology changes. Background IP of each party remains vested in that party. Foreground IP created specifically for the JV vests in the JV or is licensed to it according to an ownership matrix, subject to pre‑existing rights and approved field‑of‑use limitations.

## Parties – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
The Agreement is entered into between Tata Sons Private Limited, a company incorporated under the laws of India with its registered office at Bombay House, Mumbai, and the Service Provider (identified only as "Service Provider" in the document). Each party is referred to individually as a "Party" and collectively as the "Parties". The opening clause establishes the identity, corporate status and address of Tata Sons, and incorporates the Service Provider’s heirs, executors and administrators.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> "Tata Sons Private Limited, a company incorporated under laws of India and having its registered office at Bombay House, 24 Homi Mody Street, Mumbai 400 001 (hereinafter referred to as \"TATA\")"
> "(hereinafter, referred to as \"Service Provider\" which expression shall include unless repugnant to the context, his/her heirs, executors and administrators)\"

## Definitions – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 1.1 provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Agreement, including "Agreement", "Arbitral Tribunal", "Confidential Information", "Effective Date", "Force Majeure Event", "Intellectual Property", "Service Fee", and "TATA Manager". These definitions set the interpretative framework for the parties’ rights and obligations.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> "\"Agreement\" means this Agreement, together with the Schedules and Annexures attached hereto, as may be amended from time to time;"
> "\"Confidential Information\" of any Party shall include without limitation any and all materials, trade secrets, intellectual property, know-how, formulae, processes, algorithms, ideas, strategies, inventions, data, innovations, network configurations, system architecture, designs, flow charts, drawings, proprietary information, business and marketing plans, financial information, operational information, business methods, underwriting ideas and information and all other non‑public information, material or data relating to the past, current and /or future business and operations of such Party;"

## Scope of Services – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 2 obligates the Service Provider to render the Services from the Effective Date in accordance with Schedule I. The Services are described as a comprehensive audit of the Tata Review’s magazine design and editorial approach, with detailed sub‑scopes for design and content audit. The clause emphasizes that time is of the essence and that the Service Provider must obtain all necessary permits and licenses.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> "The Parties hereby agree that Service Provider shall, from the Effective Date, in terms of this Agreement, render services to TATA in accordance with the details and timelines, as more particularly set out in Schedule I hereto (\"Services\")."
> "The Service Provider acknowledges that time is of essence for this Agreement and undertakes to provide quality professional services in a timely manner."

## Service Fee – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 3.1 states that the Service Provider will be paid the fee set out in Schedule II. Payments are exclusive of GST, which the Service Provider must mark separately on the invoice. Clause 3.2 requires tax deduction at source where applicable, with TDS certificates to be furnished. Schedule II further details reimbursement of travel expenses and a 20 % sourcing fee on stock photographs.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> "In consideration of the Service Provider providing the Services, a fee as set out in Schedule II (\"Service Fee\") shall be payable to the Service Provider."
> "Payments shall be due within 30 days from the Invoice date."
> "Photographs purchased from stock libraries will be billed at actuals plus a 20 per cent sourcing fee."

## Project Management – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 4 allows Tata to assign a "TATA Manager" to coordinate with the Service Provider. Any change of the TATA Manager must be communicated in writing at least fourteen days in advance. This clause creates a single point of contact for performance review and problem resolution.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> "TATA may assign a representative (\"TATA Manager\") for coordination with the Service Provider Manager to review performance of this Agreement, resolutions of problems and other activities to facilitate success of this arrangement."
> "TATA shall send written notice to the Service Provider 14 (fourteen) days in advance about change of TATA Manager at anytime during the term of this Agreement."

## Representations and Warranties – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 5.1 contains the Service Provider’s warranties that it has the requisite rights to provide the Services, that its performance will not infringe any third‑party IP, that it complies with all applicable laws, and that it possesses all necessary licences and expertise. These representations form the basis for the indemnity obligations in Clause 11.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> "The Service Provider represents and warrants to TATA that: (a) it has the requisite rights, power and authority to provide the Services... and that possession and use of such information, specifications, data, work for hire and Services shall, at no point in time, ... constitute an infringement... of any patent, copyright, trade secret, or any other Intellectual Property Right of any third party;"
> "(b) the execution and delivery of this Agreement by it, the performance by it of its obligations hereunder and compliance by it with the provisions hereof will not violate, contravene or breach or create a default under any agreement, instrument, charter or by‑law provision, statute, regulation, judgment, ordinance, decree, writ, injunction or applicable law;"

## Intellectual Property – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 6 confirms that each Party retains ownership of its pre‑existing IP, but the Services are performed on a "work for hire" basis, giving TATA ownership of all IP created under the Agreement, including modifications and derivative works. The Service Provider must execute documents to vest those rights and may not use the work product for any other client.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> "The Service Provider acknowledges and agrees that the Services are performed and provided under this Agreement on a \"work for hire\" basis and TATA shall own all Intellectual Property rights contained in and with respect to the Services..."
> "The Service Provider shall not use any work product resulting from the Services and/or Intellectual Property of TATA in any manner whatsoever for itself or for any client other than TATA, at anytime."

## Force Majeure – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 7.1 allows either party to be excused from performance for a Force Majeure Event, provided the event is notified and its likely duration disclosed. If performance does not resume within thirty days after the event, the non‑affected party may terminate. Clause 7.2 requires both parties to use reasonable efforts to perform obligations during the suspension.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> "If performance is not resumed within 30 (Thirty) days after the Force Majeure Event, then the Non-Force Majeure Party may terminate this Agreement."
> "On the occurrence of any Force Majeure Event, both Parties shall use reasonable efforts to perform the obligations under this Agreement during the period of suspension."

## Term and Termination – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 8.1 sets the fixed term from 01 June 2025 to 31 March 2026, subject to mutual written extension. Clause 8.3‑8.4 list termination rights: (a) mutual agreement; (b) Force Majeure; (c) TATA’s unilateral notice of thirty days; (d) material breach not remedied within ten days; (e) insolvency events with a sixty‑day cure period. Upon termination, the Service Provider must return all Confidential Information within seven business days. The clause also preserves accrued rights.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> "This Agreement shall be effective from 01 June 2025 and shall remain valid till March 31, 2026 unless mutually extended by the Parties in writing or terminated earlier pursuant to terms hereof (\"Term\")."
> "(c) by TATA by providing the Service Provider with written notice of 30 (thirty) days;"
> "(d) by TATA if the Service Provider is in breach of its material obligations ... and which breach has not been remedied within 10 (ten) days of receipt of notice of such breach from TATA;"
> "Upon termination of this Agreement the Service Provider shall, within 7 (seven) business days from termination, return to TATA all Confidential Information of TATA in possession of the Service Provider."

## Confidentiality – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 9 obligates each Party to keep the other’s Confidential Information secret, using reasonable efforts, and to disclose it only with consent or as required by law. The confidentiality obligation survives for two years after termination. The clause also requires the Service Provider to comply with data‑privacy laws (Clause 14.9).

**Supporting Quotes:**
> "Each Party shall ... keep confidential ... any Confidential Information which is in its possession or which it acquires in relation to the other Party pursuant to this Agreement and shall not use or disclose such Confidential Information except (i) with the consent of such other Party; and (ii) for the purpose of this Agreement."
> "Such obligation of each Party shall continue for a period of 2 (two) years after termination of this Agreement."

## Governing Law and Jurisdiction – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 10 states that the Agreement is governed by the laws of India, expressly excluding conflict‑of‑laws principles, and that the courts at Mumbai, India have exclusive jurisdiction over any disputes arising under the Agreement.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> "this agreement shall be governed and interpreted by and construed in accordance with the laws of India, without giving effect, if applicable, to the principles of conflict of laws... the courts at Mumbai, India shall have exclusive jurisdiction to determine any issue arising out of this agreement between the parties."

## Indemnity – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 11 requires the Service Provider to indemnify TATA and its affiliates against any claims, losses, damages or expenses arising from (i) breach of the Service Provider’s representations and warranties, (ii) breach of any contractual obligation, or (iii) third‑party IP infringement claims. The indemnified parties include directors, employees, representatives and agents.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> "The Service Provider shall indemnify and hold TATA, its affiliates and their respective directors, employees, representatives and agents (\"Indemnified Parties\") harmless from and against any claims, demands, loss, damage or expense suffered or incurred by the Indemnified Parties as a result of (i) breach of representations and warranties made by the Service Provider under this Agreement; (ii) breach of any obligation of the Service Provider under this Agreement; and/or (iii) claims for infringement of Intellectual Property of third parties."

## Limitation of Liability – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 12 limits both Parties’ liability by excluding indirect or consequential loss, loss of profit, goodwill, business opportunity or anticipated savings. No monetary cap is specified, but the exclusion of certain loss types narrows exposure.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> "Neither Party shall be liable for indirect or consequential loss or damage, loss of profit, goodwill, business opportunity or anticipated saving arising under or in connection with this Agreement."

## Assignment and Sub‑contracting – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 13 prohibits the Service Provider from assigning its rights or sub‑contracting its obligations without TATA’s prior written consent, while retaining liability for any sub‑contracted work.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> "The Service Provider shall not (i) assign its rights and obligations; and/or (ii) sub‑contract the performance of its obligations, under this Agreement without the prior written consent of TATA. The Service Provider shall continue to be liable to TATA for any sub‑contracted work."

## Notices – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 14.3 details the method of service of notices: written, signed, delivered by personal delivery, facsimile (with receipt), or prepaid post, deemed given upon delivery or transmission, or after seven days if posted. Notices must be sent to the addresses specified in the Agreement or any later address communicated in writing.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> "Any notice or other communication to be given by one Party to any other Party under, or in connection with, this Agreement shall be made in writing and signed by or on behalf of the Party giving it. It shall be served by letter or facsimile transmission ... and shall be deemed to be duly given or made when delivered (in the case of personal delivery), at the time of transmission (in the case of facsimile transmission...), or 7 (seven) days after being dispatched in the post, postage prepaid..."

## Survival Clauses – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 14.11 enumerates the provisions that survive expiry or termination: representations and warranties, IP, term and termination clauses, confidentiality, governing law, dispute resolution, indemnity, limitation of liability, notices, data privacy, anti‑corruption, and the clause itself. This ensures continued enforceability of key obligations post‑termination.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> "Clauses 5 (Representations and Warranties), 6 (Intellectual Property), 8.3 and 8.4 (Term and Termination), 9 (Confidentiality), 10 (Governing Law and Jurisdiction), 11 (Dispute Resolution), 12 (Indemnity), 13 (Limitation of Liability), 15.3 (Notices), 15.9 (Data Privacy), 15.1 (Anti‑Corruption) and this Clause 15.11 shall survive the expiry or termination of this Agreement."

The agreement is entered into between Tata Consumer Products Limited (the "Tata" side) and Meridian Portfolio Labs LLP (the "Service Provider"). **Common Enforcement Patterns in the Tata Sons and Tata Power Solar judgments**

| Enforcement Element | Presence in Tata Sons Judgment | Presence in Tata Power Solar Judgment | How the Element Is Described (common wording) |
|---------------------|--------------------------------|----------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| **Injunction** | Injunction restraining defendants from using the “TATA” mark and similar marks; permanent injunction granted (paragraph 84(i)‑(iv))【1】,【2】 | Interim injunction restraining defendants (and affiliates) from using “TATA POWER SOLAR” or similar marks【13】 | “restrained from using … any deceptively similar mark” |
| **Undertaking** | Defendants undertook never to use the impugned packaging; court accepted and bound parties【3】 | Plaintiffs (and implicitly defendants) required to give “usual undertakings as to costs and accuracy of technical evidence”【9】; also “liberty … to place on record additional mirror domains … without fresh suit”【14】 | Parties bound by an undertaking/undertakings to refrain from further infringement |
| **Takedown / Platform Obligations** | Registrars, hosting intermediaries, platform operators must act on authenticated copies, takedown URLs, block payment handles, preserve logs【10】 | Registrars and hosting platforms must lock/suspend identified domains, preserve KYC/pay‑ment/traffic logs, and may seek further directions for mirror domains【11】,【14】 | “immediate takedown … preservation of subscriber records, KYC material, payment details, traffic logs …” |
| **Destruction of Infringing Goods** | Seized goods to be destroyed by defendant in presence of plaintiffs’ representatives within 15 days【4】 | No explicit destruction provision found in the Tata Power Solar excerpts. |
| **Damages / Nominal Cost** | Court applied Philips chart, classified defendant as “first‑time innocent infringer” and ordered nominal cost of ₹1,00,000 only【5】 | No damages or cost award language appears in the Tata Power Solar excerpts. |
| **Court‑Fee Refund** | 100 % refund of court fee ordered, relying on Sec. 16 & 16A of Court Fees Act and a Supreme Court judgment【6】 | No court‑fee refund provision appears in the Tata Power Solar excerpts. |
| **Treatment of First‑Time Infringer** | Explicitly labeled defendant a “first‑time innocent infringer” and limited award to nominal cost【5】 | No explicit classification of the defendant as a first‑time infringer in the Tata Power Solar excerpts. |

**Summary of Overlap**

- Both judgments employ **injunctive relief** (permanent or interim) to stop use of the Tata marks and any deceptively similar marks.  
- Both require **undertakings** from the parties, binding them to refrain from further infringement and to comply with procedural directions.  
- Both impose **obligations on registrars/hosting platforms** to takedown infringing URLs, block payment handles, and preserve relevant data, with a mechanism to address newly discovered mirror domains.  

Elements that appear **only in the Tata Sons** judgment are **destruction of seized goods, a nominal damages/cost award, a full court‑fee refund, and the explicit “first‑time innocent infringer” classification**. No comparable provisions are present in the Tata Power Solar excerpts.  

Thus, the common enforcement pattern centers on **injunctions, undertakings, and digital‑platform takedown/ preservation orders**, while the Tata Sons case adds additional remedial measures concerning physical goods, nominal damages, fee refund, and first‑time infringer treatment.

## Obligations of Registrars and Platform Operators – TataPowerSolar (Court Judgment)
The order imposes a duty on registrars and hosting platforms to (a) lock and suspend the identified infringing domains, (b) preserve registrant, KYC, payment, traffic‑log and takedown records, and (c) produce such information before the Court if required. They are also empowered to seek further directions for newly discovered mirror domains without initiating a fresh suit.

## Plaintiffs’ Undertakings – TataPowerSolar (Court Judgment)
The plaintiffs are required to give the usual undertakings regarding costs and the accuracy of the technical evidence presented, and to file further pleadings, affidavits of admission and denial, and any applications for additional relief on the next listed date.

## Court’s Observations on Digital Environment – TataPowerSolar (Court Judgment)
The Court emphasized that the digital environment enables rapid creation of mirror domains and cloned pages, necessitating a flexible and technology‑conscious interim remedy to preserve the efficacy of the proceedings.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> This Court is also mindful that the digital environment permits rapid migration to mirror domains, cloned pages, modified email addresses, and repeat misuse through fresh registrants.
> Any effective interim remedy must therefore be practical, technology‑conscious, and sufficiently flexible to preserve the efficacy of the proceedings.

## Balance of Convenience – TataPowerSolar (Court Judgment)
The Court held that denying the injunction would cause immediate and irreparable injury to the plaintiffs because consumers could continue to part with personal data and money. Conversely, the defendants have not shown any substantial prejudice that would outweigh the plaintiffs' interest, especially given their non‑appearance.

**Supporting Quotes:**

## Issues – TataPowerSolar (Court Judgment)
The Court needed to determine (1) whether the defendants' use of the contested marks and domain names amounts to trademark infringement, passing off, dilution and unfair misrepresentation; (2) whether the balance of convenience favours granting an interim injunction; and (3) what specific restraining orders are appropriate in the digital environment.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> The impugned conduct amounts, prima facie, to trademark infringement, passing off, dilution, and unfair misrepresentation.
> The balance of convenience is in favour of Tata Power Solar Systems Limited.

The recitals explain that Tata’s public disclosures on capacity expansion and a net‑zero agenda create a need for external advisory support with measurable deliverables, confidentiality, IP ownership and compliance with the Tata Code of Conduct.

**Supporting Quotes:**

> Public Tata Steel information highlights capacity expansion, downstream manufacturing breadth, and a long‑term net‑zero agenda, which require carefully documented external support arrangements for feasibility, sequencing, and vendor coordination.

**Subject:** Key Risks in Service Agreement 3 (Helios) & Suggested Legal Amendments  

Dear [Recipient],

Please find below a concise, business‑focused overview of the principal risks identified in **Service Agreement 3 (Helios Grid Advisory Private Limited)** together with the recommended contractual changes to mitigate those risks.

| **Risk Area** | **What the Agreement Currently Provides** | **Why It Is a Risk** | **Proposed Legal Change** |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Intellectual Property (IP) Ownership** | All deliverables created for Tata “shall vest in Tata upon creation” and the Service Provider must grant a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty‑free licence for any pre‑existing material it incorporates【7】. | The clause does not require the Service Provider to obtain written assignments from any subcontractors, which could leave Tata exposed to third‑party claims. | Add a representation that the Service Provider will secure and provide evidence of all necessary licences/assignments from its subcontractors for any incorporated pre‑existing material. |
| **Indemnity Scope & Caps** | The Service Provider indemnifies Tata for bodily injury, property damage, infringement, data misuse, breach of confidentiality, fraud, wilful misconduct, and law violations. Ordinary commercial claims are capped at the financial cap in the SOW, but the cap does **not** apply to the uncapped categories【8】. | Uncapped exposure for fraud, wilful misconduct, infringement, etc., could result in unlimited liability for Tata if a claim arises. | Insert a **maximum aggregate liability** for the uncapped categories (e.g., a multiple of the contract value) while preserving the existing carve‑outs for fraud and wilful misconduct. |
| **Limitation of Liability** | Liability for ordinary commercial claims is limited to the negotiated financial cap; uncapped categories remain as above【8】. | The current cap may be too low relative to the value of the services, leaving Tata under‑compensated for losses. | Negotiate a higher cap for ordinary claims (e.g., 150 % of the total fees) and ensure the cap is expressed as a specific monetary amount rather than “subject to the SOW”. |
| **Force‑Majeure Termination** | Either party may terminate if performance does not resume within **30 days** after a Force‑Majeure Event【5】. | A short 30‑day window may force premature termination for events that are prolonged but manageable (e.g., pandemic‑related delays). | Extend the notice period to **60 days** and require the non‑affected party to act in good faith to mitigate the impact before termination is exercised. |
| **Termination Notice & Cure Periods** | Tata may terminate for convenience with notice; material breach by the Service Provider can be terminated after **10 days** cure period【8】. | A 10‑day cure period may be insufficient for complex service failures, exposing Tata to abrupt service disruption. | Increase the cure period to **15 days** and require the Service Provider to submit a remediation plan within 5 days of breach notice. |
| **Audit Rights** | Tata may withhold disputed amounts, set‑off liquidated damages, and audit the Service Provider’s books, records, and supporting evidence【5】. | The audit clause does not specify a reasonable notice period or the scope of audit, which could lead to operational friction. | Add a provision that Tata will give **10 business days’ written notice** before any audit and that audits will be limited to records directly related to fees, compliance, and subcontracting. |
| **Confidentiality Survival** | Confidentiality obligations survive for **two years** after termination【5】. | Certain sensitive data (e.g., AI training data) may require longer protection. | Extend the confidentiality survival period to **five years** for any Tata Confidential Information relating to proprietary technology or data. |
| **Governing Law & Dispute Forum** | Governed by Indian law; arbitration seated in **New Delhi** after escalation, with interim relief from courts【9】. | The arbitration seat may be less convenient for Tata’s Mumbai‑based team. | Change the arbitration seat to **Mumbai** to align with Tata’s primary operations and reduce travel/logistical costs. |
| **Key Personnel Replacement** | Service Provider cannot replace key personnel without Tata’s prior written consent, except for resignation, illness, or emergency【6】. | No explicit timeline for proposing replacements may cause delays. | Require the Service Provider to propose an equivalent replacement **within 3 business days** of any key‑person departure. |

### Next Steps
1. **Draft amendment language** reflecting the above changes.  
2. **Circulate** the proposed amendments to Helios for review.  
3. **Schedule a call** with the Helios legal team to discuss any concerns and finalize the revised agreement.

Please let me know if you need any further detail or a revised draft of the amendment clauses.

Best regards,  
[Your Name]  
Legal Counsel – Tata Group  

---

**References**  

[7] SA‑Helios (Service Agreement), Clause 5 – IP ownership & licence.  
[8] SA‑Helios (Service Agreement), Clause 7 – Indemnity & limitation of liability.  
[5] SA‑Helios (Service Agreement), Clause 2 & 5 – Force Majeure & termination.  
[6] SA‑Helios (Service Agreement), Clause 3 – Personnel replacement.  
[9] SA‑Helios (Service Agreement), Clause 8 – Governing law & dispute resolution.

**Reserved‑Matters Analysis – Tata Steel Ltd. & SteelLoop Resource Recovery Pvt Ltd. (JV3‑SteelLoop)**  

| Corporate decision | Treatment under the JV Agreement | Required board vote / consent |
|--------------------|-----------------------------------|--------------------------------|
| **Capital raises / new indebtedness** | Listed explicitly in the “Reserved matters” identified for Tata‑consent items (capital raises, new indebtedness)【1】 | **Unanimous board approval** (or at least the Tata‑nominee quorum plus consent of the other party) – the agreement ties these matters to the “reserved‑matter schedule” and mandates Tata’s consent, which in practice is satisfied only by a unanimous board vote because no lower‑threshold alternative is provided. |
| **Business‑plan deviations / material deviations from the approved annual business plan** | The annual business plan must be prepared each year and “material deviation shall require board approval in accordance with the reserved‑matter matrix”【2】 | **Special‑majority (reserved‑matter) approval** – the matrix requires the presence of a Tata nominee and a non‑Tata consenting member; in practice this means a **qualified majority** (typically ≥ 75 % of the board) or **unanimous** if the matrix is drafted that way. |
| **IP assignments / transfer of core technology** | Reserved matters include “IP assignments”【1】 | **Unanimous board approval** (or Tata‑nominee quorum) because IP is a strategic asset and the counsel’s recommendation is to “hard‑wire Tata nominee quorum” for such items. |
| **Related‑party transactions** | Explicitly listed among reserved matters (related‑party transactions)【1】 | **Unanimous board approval** (or Tata‑nominee quorum) – the agreement prevents fragmentation and requires full board consent for any related‑party deal. |
| **Litigation settlements (material claims)** | “Litigation settlements” are a reserved matter【1】 | **Unanimous board approval** (or Tata‑nominee quorum) – settlement of material claims is treated as a strategic decision requiring the full board’s assent. |
| **Move into competitor‑aligned business lines** | Reserved matter “any move into competitor‑aligned business lines”【1】 | **Unanimous board approval** (or Tata‑nominee quorum) – such a shift would affect the JV’s core purpose and therefore triggers the highest consent level. |
| **Major capital expenditure (CAPEX) beyond thresholds** | While not quoted verbatim, the “reserved‑matter matrix” governs “major capital expenditure” in analogous SHA‑3‑SteelCircle and is reflected in the JV’s governance principles that tie CAPEX to board approval【3】 | **Special‑majority** – the matrix typically requires the Tata‑nominee quorum plus a non‑Tata member, effectively a qualified majority. |
| **Long‑term offtake commitments / pricing policy changes with strategic effect** | Enumerated in other SHA examples (e.g., SHA‑3‑SteelCircle) and consistent with the JV’s “exit triggers” and “budget approval discipline”【4】 | **Unanimous board approval** (or Tata‑nominee quorum) because they affect financing discipline and strategic control. |
| **Technology non‑compete limitations / licensing to competitor‑controlled groups** | Covered under the “technology non‑compete limitations” governance principle and reserved‑matter lists (e.g., licensing to competitor‑controlled groups in SHA‑LexPulse)【5】 | **Unanimous board approval** – any waiver or change requires the full board (or Tata‑nominee quorum) to avoid breach of the non‑compete. |
| **Brand usage / external communication of names, logos, trade‑dress** | Requires “prior approval” under the exclusivity and brand controls clause【6】 | **Special‑majority** – approval must be obtained from the board, with at least one Tata nominee present; in practice this is treated as a reserved matter needing Tata’s consent. |
| **Exit triggers (change of control, insolvency, sanctions, persistent KPI failure, uncured breach, extended force majeure, illegality)** | Listed under “Exit triggers”【7】 | **Unanimous board approval** to invoke an exit, as these are fundamental events that can dissolve the JV. |

### Risk Classification  

| Decision | Risk if consent not obtained | Classification |
|----------|-----------------------------|----------------|
| Capital raises / new indebtedness | Dilution, breach of financing covenants, loss of control | **High** |
| Business‑plan deviations | Mis‑aligned spending, KPI failure, breach of reserved‑matter matrix | **Medium‑High** |
| IP assignments | Loss of core technology, competitive disadvantage | **High** |
| Related‑party transactions | Conflict of interest, regulatory scrutiny | **Medium** |
| Litigation settlements | Uncontrolled exposure, adverse precedent | **Medium‑High** |
| Move into competitor‑aligned lines | Strategic drift, breach of exclusivity | **High** |
| Major CAPEX | Over‑investment, cash‑flow strain | **Medium** |
| Long‑term offtake / pricing changes | Revenue volatility, market lock‑in | **Medium** |
| Technology non‑compete / licensing | IP leakage, competition | **High** |
| Brand usage | Reputation damage, brand dilution | **Medium** |
| Exit triggers | Unplanned dissolution, loss of value | **High** |

### Gaps & Missing Protections  

* The JV text does **not** spell out a **numeric quorum** (e.g., 75 % of board) for the reserved‑matter matrix; relying solely on “Tata‑nominee quorum” may be insufficient if the non‑Tata side holds a majority of seats.  
* No explicit **cap on liability** for ordinary under‑performance is provided; while enhanced remedies exist for fraud etc., a standard cap would align with market practice.  
* The “cooling‑off” and “mediation” steps in deadlock resolution are described, but there is no **binding arbitration** clause if mediation fails, which is common in JV structures.  

### Recommendations  

1. **Insert a precise quorum clause** for all reserved matters: e.g., “unanimous consent of all directors, or at least a qualified majority of 75 % including all Tata nominees.”  
2. **Codify the reserved‑matter matrix** in an annex, listing each decision and the exact voting threshold (unanimous vs. special majority).  
3. **Add a liability cap** for ordinary business risks (e.g., “liability limited to the aggregate capital contributions”) while preserving the enhanced remedies for fraud, misconduct, etc.  
4. **Include a binding arbitration provision** (e.g., ICC Rules, seat in Mumbai) to follow mediation, ensuring enforceable resolution of deadlocks.  
5. **Require written board minutes** for any approval of brand usage, IP assignment, or related‑party transaction to create an audit trail.  

**Conclusion** – Under the JV3‑SteelLoop agreement, the corporate decisions that **require unanimous board approval or a special‑majority consent** are: capital raises, new indebtedness, major CAPEX, business‑plan deviations, IP assignments, related‑party transactions, material litigation settlements, moves into competitor‑aligned lines, long‑term offtake or pricing changes, technology non‑compete waivers, and any invocation of exit triggers. Ensuring that the board’s voting rules are explicitly defined and that a detailed reserved‑matter matrix is annexed will mitigate the high‑risk exposure associated with these strategic decisions.

**Reserved‑Matters Review – Tata Steel Limited / SteelLoop Resource Recovery Private Limited JV**

| Corporate Decision | Approval Requirement | Source in Context |
|--------------------|----------------------|-------------------|
| **Capital raises / additional capital contributions** | Unanimous board approval (or “unanimous board vote”) | “Any request for additional capital contributions must be approved by a unanimous vote of the Board of Directors.” – *Board Approval for Material Deviations* and *Board of Directors of HASG LLC* clauses【1】 |
| **Business‑plan deviations (including material changes to CAPEX, operating budget, technical milestones, capacity ramps, sourcing assumptions, revenue targets, customer‑concentration thresholds)** | Unanimous board approval (or board approval per the Reserved Matters matrix) | “Material deviations shall require board approval in accordance with the reserved matter matrix.” – *Annual Business Plan* and *Reserved Matters Matrix – JVReVolt* clauses【2】 |
| **Intellectual‑property (IP) assignments / transfer of core source code** | Unanimous board approval (or “Tata‑consent” item) | “Reserved matters should cover … IP assignments …” – *Reserved Matters – Legal Opinion*【3】 |
| **Related‑party transactions** | Unanimous board approval (or “Tata‑consent” item) | Same as above – *Reserved Matters – Legal Opinion*【3】 |
| **Litigation settlements / settlement of privacy incidents** | Unanimous board approval (or “Tata‑consent” item) | Same as above – *Reserved Matters – Legal Opinion*【3】 |
| **New indebtedness (including borrowing, guarantees, security interests)** | Unanimous board approval (or “Tata‑consent” item) | Same as above – *Reserved Matters – Legal Opinion*【3】 |
| **Entry into competitor‑aligned business lines (including licensing to competitor‑controlled groups, model‑training or dataset‑use changes that would benefit a competitor)** | Unanimous board approval (or “Tata‑consent” item) | Same as above – *Reserved Matters – Legal Opinion* and *SHA‑LexPulse* clauses【3】【4】 |
| **Changes to technology / non‑compete limitations that affect the JV’s core tech pathway** | Unanimous board approval (implied by “technology non‑compete limitations” in governance principles) | “The JV shall operate under governance principles that include … technology non‑compete limitations …” – *Governance Framework – JV3‑SteelLoop*【5】 |
| **Brand usage that deviates from approved protocols** | Board/qualified‑majority consent (not necessarily unanimous, but requires prior approval) | “Use of names, logos … requires prior approval.” – *Exclusivity and Brand Controls – JV3‑SteelLoop*【6】 |

### Assessment

- **Unanimous Board Approval Required** – The JV explicitly ties **any additional capital call** and **material deviations from the approved business plan** to a **unanimous board vote** (see the “unanimous vote” language in the board‑approval provisions).  
- **Special‑Majority / Tata‑Consent Items** – The legal opinion earmarks a set of **reserved matters** that must obtain **Tata‑consent**, effectively a **special majority** (often defined as at least one Tata nominee plus a non‑Tata member, per the SHA‑LexPulse quorum rule). These include capital raises, IP assignments, related‑party deals, litigation settlements, new indebtedness, and moves into competitor‑aligned activities.  
- **Governance Controls** – While brand‑usage approvals and technology non‑compete limitations are also controlled, the documents do not stipulate unanimity; they require **pre‑approval** under the brand‑governance protocol or the governance principles, which typically means a **board or designated committee majority**.

### Risk Classification

| Decision Category | Risk if Unapproved | Classification |
|-------------------|-------------------|----------------|
| Capital raises / additional contributions | Dilution, funding shortfall, breach of JV covenant | **High** – unanimity required; failure triggers default. |
| Business‑plan deviations | Misaligned strategy, budget overruns, HSE non‑compliance | **High** – material deviation without board sign‑off breaches the Reserved Matters matrix. |
| IP assignments / core source code transfer | Loss of proprietary technology, competitive leakage | **Medium‑High** – special‑majority required; breach could impair JV value. |
| Related‑party transactions | Conflict of interest, regulatory scrutiny | **Medium** – special‑majority protects against abuse. |
| Litigation settlements / privacy incident settlements | Uncontrolled liability exposure | **Medium** – special‑majority ensures oversight. |
| New indebtedness | Over‑leverage, covenant breach | **Medium** – special‑majority needed. |
| Entry into competitor‑aligned lines | Strategic conflict, erosion of exclusivity | **Medium** – special‑majority safeguards Tata’s strategic interests. |
| Technology non‑compete breaches | Competitive disadvantage, IP loss | **Medium** – governance principle but not expressly unanimity. |
| Brand usage outside protocol | Reputation damage, brand dilution | **Low‑Medium** – procedural approval required, lower financial impact. |

### Recommendations

1. **Confirm the exact voting threshold for each reserved matter** in the final JV agreement (e.g., whether “special majority” equals a Tata‑nominee plus one non‑Tata, or a higher super‑majority).  
2. **Insert a detailed Reserved‑Matter Schedule** that cross‑references each decision type with its required approval level (unanimous vs. special‑majority) to avoid ambiguity.  
3. **Add a “Board‑Resolution Template”** for capital calls and business‑plan amendments that explicitly requires signatures of all five directors (or the unanimity clause) to enforce compliance.  
4. **Negotiate a “Cooling‑Off” clause** for capital‑raise decisions, allowing a short period for dissenting directors to raise concerns before a final vote, mitigating the risk of rushed unanimous approvals.  
5. **Ensure the escalation protocol** (deadlock resolution) explicitly covers situations where unanimity cannot be reached on a reserved matter, linking to the buy‑sell or separation mechanism.  
6. **Obtain a side‑letter** confirming that any amendment to the Reserved‑Matter Schedule itself will require the same unanimity/special‑majority, preventing future dilution of control.  

**Conclusion:** Under the Tata Steel / SteelLoop JV, **any capital raise, additional capital contribution, or material deviation from the approved business plan must be approved unanimously by the board**. All other listed corporate actions—IP assignments, related‑party transactions, litigation settlements, new indebtedness, and moves into competitor‑aligned business lines—require **special‑majority consent** (effectively Tata‑consent as defined in the legal opinion). Proper documentation and clear voting thresholds are essential to mitigate high‑risk exposure.

The Agreement is entered into between Tata Sons Private Limited, a company incorporated under the laws of India with its registered office at Bombay House, Mumbai, and the Service Provider (identified only as "Service Provider" in the document). Each party is referred to individually as a "Party" and collectively as the "Parties". The opening clause establishes the identity, corporate status and address of Tata Sons, and incorporates the Service Provider’s heirs, executors and administrators.

**Supporting Quotes:**

## Definitions – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 1.1 provides definitions for key terms used throughout the Agreement, including "Agreement", "Arbitral Tribunal", "Confidential Information", "Effective Date", "Force Majeure Event", "Intellectual Property", "Service Fee", and "TATA Manager". These definitions set the interpretative framework for the parties’ rights and obligations.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> "\"Agreement\" means this Agreement, together with the Schedules and Annexures attached hereto, as may be amended from time to time;"
> "\"Confidential Information\" of any Party shall include without limitation any and all materials, trade secrets, intellectual property, know-how, formulae, processes, algorithms, ideas, strategies, inventions, data, innovations, network configurations, system architecture, designs, flow charts, drawings, proprietary information, business and marketing plans, financial information, operational information, business methods, underwriting ideas and information and all other non‑public information, material or data relating to the past, current and /or future business and operations of such Party;"

## Scope of Services – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 2 obligates the Service Provider to render the Services from the Effective Date in accordance with Schedule I. The Services are described as a comprehensive audit of the Tata Review’s magazine design and editorial approach, with detailed sub‑scopes for design and content audit. The clause emphasizes that time is of the essence and that the Service Provider must obtain all necessary permits and licenses.

**Supporting Quotes:**
> "The Parties hereby agree that Service Provider shall, from the Effective Date, in terms of this Agreement, render services to TATA in accordance with the details and timelines, as more particularly set out in Schedule I hereto (\"Services\")."

## Service Fee – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 3.1 states that the Service Provider will be paid the fee set out in Schedule II. Payments are exclusive of GST, which the Service Provider must mark separately on the invoice. Clause 3.2 requires tax deduction at source where applicable, with TDS certificates to be furnished. Schedule II further details reimbursement of travel expenses and a 20 % sourcing fee on stock photographs.

**Supporting Quotes:**

**Supporting Quotes:**

Clause 5.1 contains the Service Provider’s warranties that it has the requisite rights to provide the Services, that its performance will not infringe any third‑party IP, that it complies with all applicable laws, and that it possesses all necessary licences and expertise. These representations form the basis for the indemnity obligations in Clause 11.

**Supporting Quotes:**

## Intellectual Property – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 6 confirms that each Party retains ownership of its pre‑existing IP, but the Services are performed on a "work for hire" basis, giving TATA ownership of all IP created under the Agreement, including modifications and derivative works. ## Force Majeure – SA-Tata (Service Agreement)
Clause 7.1 allows either party to be excused from performance for a Force Majeure Event, provided the event is notified and its likely duration disclosed. **Common enforcement patterns in the Tata brand judgments**

| Enforcement element | Present in **Tata Sons** | Present in **TataPowerSolar** | Common to both? |
|---------------------|---------------------------|--------------------------------|-----------------|
| **Injunction** (interim/permanent) | “ex‑parte ad interim injunction …” and “permanent injunction …” restraining use of the “TATA” mark. | “interim injunction … restraining the defendants …” (balance of convenience discussion) | ✅ |
| **Undertakings** | Defendants “undertake to never use the impugned packaging …” and file an affidavit. | Plaintiffs “shall comply with the usual undertakings …” (costs, accuracy of technical evidence). | ✅ |
| **Takedown / Registrar duties** | No mention of domain or registrar takedown. | Registrars/hosting platforms must lock/suspend infringing domains and preserve records. | ❌ (only in TataPowerSolar) |
| **Destruction of infringing goods** | “goods seized … shall be destroyed by the defendant …” | No reference to destruction. | ❌ (only in Tata Sons) |
| **Damages** | “first‑time innocent infringer … nominal cost of ₹1,00,000/‑” and discussion of damages claim. | No damages discussion. | ❌ (only in Tata Sons) |
| **Court‑fee refund** | “refund 100 % Court Fee … within six weeks …” | No refund order. | ❌ (only in Tata Sons) |
| **Treatment of first‑time infringers** | Explicit classification as “first‑time innocent infringer” with nominal cost. | No classification. | ❌ (only in Tata Sons) |

**Summary**

Both Tata Sons and TataPowerSolar judgments employ **injunctions** and **court‑mandated undertakings** as core enforcement tools. TataPowerSolar adds **registrar/domain takedown obligations**, whereas Tata Sons adds **destruction of seized goods**, a **nominal‑damage regime for first‑time infringers**, and a **full court‑fee refund**. The latter three elements are not reflected in the TataPowerSolar decision.

**References**

[1] Tata Sons (Court Judgment), Procedural History – ex‑parte ad interim injunction dated 31 January 2024.  
[2] Tata Sons (Court Judgment), Permanent Injunction – decree of permanent injunction paragraph 84 (i)‑(iv).  
[3] Tata Sons (Court Judgment), Defendants' Undertaking – defendants undertake never to use impugned packaging.  
[4] TataPowerSolar (Court Judgment), Procedural History – interim injunction considered under trademark interlocutory relief.  
[5] TataPowerSolar (Court Judgment), Plaintiffs’ Undertakings – plaintiffs to give usual undertakings as to costs and technical evidence.  
[6] TataPowerSolar (Court Judgment), Obligations of Registrars and Platform Operators – duty to lock/suspend infringing domains and preserve records.  
[7] Tata Sons (Court Judgment), Destruction of Infringing Goods – seized goods to be destroyed in presence of plaintiffs.  
[8] Tata Sons (Court Judgment), Damages Framework – classification as “first‑time innocent infringer” and nominal cost award.  
[9] Tata Sons (Court Judgment), Court Fee Refund – 100 % refund of court fee within six weeks, citing Section 16 & 16A, Court Fees Act, 1870.

**Subject:** Summary of Key Risks and Suggested Legal Amendments – Service Agreement 3  

Dear [Recipient],

Below is a concise, business‑friendly overview of the principal risks identified in **Service Agreement 3** and the corresponding legal modifications we recommend to mitigate those risks.

| **Risk Area** | **Why It Matters** | **Proposed Legal Change** |
|---------------|--------------------|---------------------------|
| **IP Ownership & Work‑for‑Hire** | The agreement currently grants the service provider ownership of pre‑existing IP but does not expressly require a “work‑for‑hire” assignment for all deliverables, leaving Tata exposed to potential third‑party claims. | Insert a clause stating that all deliverables are “work for hire” and that the service provider must execute all necessary documents to vest full IP rights in Tata upon creation. |
| **Indemnity Scope** | Indemnity is limited to breach of representations, obligations, and third‑party IP infringement, but does not cover data‑misuse, confidentiality breaches, or regulatory violations. | Expand the indemnity provision to include claims arising from data misuse, breach of confidentiality, and any violation of applicable laws, mirroring the broader language used in the Helios and Redwood agreements. |
| **Limitation of Liability** | The current limitation excludes indirect loss but imposes a monetary cap tied to the last two invoices, which may be insufficient for high‑value projects. | Replace the invoice‑based cap with a fixed, reasonable monetary ceiling (e.g., ₹ [amount]) and expressly carve out uncapped liability for fraud, wilful misconduct, breach of confidentiality, and IP infringement. |
| **Force Majeure Termination** | Termination is permitted after 30 days of suspension, which may be too short for large‑scale, infrastructure‑related services. | Extend the notice period to 60 days and require the non‑affected party to provide a written cure opportunity before exercising termination rights. |
| **Assignment & Sub‑contracting** | The agreement prohibits assignment and sub‑contracting without consent but does not obligate the service provider to remain liable for subcontracted work. | Add language confirming that the service provider remains fully liable for any subcontracted work and must obtain written consent for any assignment. |
| **Confidentiality Survival** | Confidentiality survives only two years post‑termination, which may be inadequate for proprietary data. | Extend the confidentiality survival period to five years, aligning with best practice in the Meridian and Helios agreements. |
| **Governing Law & Jurisdiction** | The clause specifies exclusive jurisdiction in Mumbai but does not address interim relief. | Include a provision allowing either party to seek interim or conservatory relief from competent courts to protect confidential information or IP during disputes. |
| **Notice Requirements** | Notices are deemed given after 7 days post‑mail, which could delay critical communications. | Shorten the deemed receipt period to 5 days for postal delivery and require electronic acknowledgment for fax/email notices. |

These amendments aim to strengthen Tata’s protection, clarify responsibilities, and align the agreement with the more robust risk‑mitigation language observed in our other service contracts.

Please let me know if you would like a revised draft incorporating these changes or if you have any questions.

Best regards,  
[Your Name]  
Legal Counsel, Tata  

---  

*This summary is based solely on the excerpts provided and does not constitute legal advice.*

## ✅ Clauses Generally Acceptable (Standard, Low‑Risk)

| Clause | Why Acceptable | Example Source |
|--------|----------------|----------------|

| **Obligations of Receiving Party** – use solely for purpose, reasonable care, need‑to‑know disclosures. | Standard confidentiality duty; aligns with industry practice. | NDA‑Tata (Obligations) – “use … only in relation to the Purpose … maintain the confidentiality … same degree of care”【4】 |
| **Return/Destruction of Confidential Information** – prompt return or secure destruction on request, with certification. | Ensures data is removed after the relationship ends. | NDA‑Tata (Return) – “return or destroy … certify in writing”【5】 |

## ⚠️ Clauses Requiring Escalation (Higher Risk / Ambiguities)

| Clause | Issue / Risk | Suggested Action | Source |
|--------|--------------|------------------|--------|

| **Assignment Restrictions** – Neither party may assign without consent; Tata may assign to affiliates. | May hinder future restructuring or sale of the business. | Request a broader carve‑out for affiliates or successors. | NDA‑Tata (Assignment) – “Receiving Party shall not assign … without prior written consent”【17】 |

**VoltMetric Analytics Private Limited – Share Transfer Restrictions for Non‑Tata Shareholders**

- **Lock‑in provisions** – Shares cannot be transferred freely during the lock‑in period.  
- **Right of First Offer (ROFO)** – A shareholder wishing to sell must first offer the shares to the other shareholders on the same terms.  
- **Right of First Refusal (ROFR)** – If a shareholder receives a third‑party offer, the other shareholders have the right to purchase the shares on those terms before the sale proceeds.  
- **Tag‑along protections** – When a shareholder sells a controlling stake, the remaining shareholders may participate pro‑rata in the sale.  
- **Drag‑along mechanics** – Holders of a specified majority can compel the other shareholders to join in a sale on the same terms.  
- **Additional prohibitions** – Transfers are barred to competitors, sanctioned persons, reputationally sensitive acquirers, or any party that cannot satisfy Tata’s integrity expectations.

These provisions collectively govern how non‑Tata shareholders may transfer their equity interests.

**References**

- *SHA‑VoltMetric (Shareholders' Agreement), Transfer Restrictions* – “Shares shall be subject to lock‑in provisions, rights of first offer or refusal, tag‑along protections, drag‑along mechanics, and restrictions on transfers to competitors, sanctioned persons, reputationally sensitive acquirers, or parties unable to meet Tata's integrity expectations.”【1】

Limitation of liability (Clause 12 SA‑Tata) only excludes indirect loss, no cap. | **High** | Tata could face unlimited liability for third‑party claims arising from the Service Provider’s breach, especially where sub‑contractors are used without flow‑down indemnities. |
